note: Both sets cover the same core content of Figure 2-6 — the six cross-section materials (Medium Density Foam, Glass Triax, Glass Biax, Carbon UD, Glass Uni, Gelcoat) and the CG/GC/NA/SC marker coordinates — and both share the same internal conflict (GC x3 given as both 0.05 m and 0.0 m for the same point) plus the same material claims repeated under two condition phrasings for one figure. B adds one genuinely useful fact (cross section located at 70% span, supported by the caption) but also six redundant 'material layer' claims that simply repeat its own 'material' claims under a second attribute name. A thus delivers essentially the same correct content with far less duplication, while B's only unique gain is a caption fact already carried in A's conditions.
remarks: The text layer contains only the two captions and the footer; all legend labels, marker coordinates and the 'Section : 0.7' title come from the figure image, so the coordinate values (e.g. NA x2 = -0.1, CG x2 = -0.15, SC x2 = -0.2, GC x3 = 0.05) are plot readings that cannot be verified to better than plot resolution. Both sets contain the contradictory pair GC x3 = 0.05 m and GC x3 = 0.0 m for the same point in the same figure — at least one is a misread, and it should be resolved. Both sets also use legend labels ('CG: Mass Center', 'NA: Neutral Axes', 'SC: Generalized Shear Center', 'GC: Geometric Center') as entities and as quotes, so the quotes support the label but not the numeric values; the numbers are unsupported by any quoted text. Each material is stated twice per set under two condition spellings ('Section : 0.7' vs 'cross section at 70% span') that denote the same figure, and B compounds this with a third 'material layer' variant.
